Q: Running purrr functionals in parallel: imap A:

Over in Futureverse, you can use the new futurize package and its futurize() function - it allows you to keep your original code as-is. It works with purrr and tons of other types of calls.

In your case, use:

library(futurize)
plan(multisession)
...
d1 <- imap(sampled_ids, resamp_df, df) |> futurize()

That's it!

PS. If you prefer non-pipe syntax, you can use d1 <- futurize(imap(sampled_ids, resamp_df, df)), which is an identical call.

Details

Say you use:

library(purrr)
z <- imap(5:8, ~ runif(.y, max = .x))

You can parallelize this by piping the expression to futurize() as in:

library(purrr)

## Set up parallel workers
library(futurize)
plan(multisession)

z <- imap(5:8, ~ runif(.y, max = .x)) |> futurize(seed = TRUE)

Here we use seed = TRUE to tell futureverse to set up proper parallel RNG. If there are no random numbers generated, it's just ... |> futurize().

You've got several other backends to choose from, e.g. plan(future.mirai::mirai_multisession).
